dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For ell,f : Fin n -> R, this is the ratio (sum over all i of |ell_i f_i|) / |sum over all i of ell_i f_i|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the sensitivity factor multiplied by epsilon on the right-hand side. The nonzero baseline hypothesis ensures that its denominator is nonzero.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For ell,f : Fin n -> R, this is the weighted linear functional S(ell,f) = sum over all i in Fin n of ell_i f_i.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the baseline value, the perturbed value S(ell,f+deltaF), their difference, the normalizing denominator, and the hypothesis that the baseline value is nonzero.

binders: n is an implicitly universally quantified natural number.
ell, f, and deltaF are universally quantified functions Fin n -> R, equivalently arbitrary real vectors with n coordinates.
epsilon is a universally quantified real number.
hypotheses: For every coordinate i in Fin n, |deltaF_i| <= epsilon |f_i|.
The baseline weighted sum S(ell,f) = sum_i ell_i f_i is nonzero.
conclusions: The normalized exact change satisfies |S(ell,f+deltaF) - S(ell,f)| / |S(ell,f)| <= epsilon (sum_i |ell_i f_i| / |S(ell,f)|).
mathematical_definitions: The coordinate set Fin n is the n-element set of indices i = 0, ..., n-1.
S(ell,x) denotes the exact weighted sum sum_i ell_i x_i.
The perturbed vector f+deltaF is defined coordinatewise by (f+deltaF)_i = f_i + deltaF_i.
The factor LocalDef001(ell,f) is K(ell,f) = (sum_i |ell_i f_i|) / |sum_i ell_i f_i|.
By exact distributivity of real finite sums, S(ell,f+deltaF) - S(ell,f) = sum_i ell_i deltaF_i, so the numerator is |sum_i ell_i deltaF_i|.
Every absolute value in the proposition is scalar real absolute value; no vector norm is used.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite dimension n, every real weight vector ell, every real vector f, every real perturbation deltaF, and every real epsilon, if each perturbation component has magnitude at most epsilon times the magnitude of the corresponding component of f, and if the weighted sum sum_i ell_i f_i is nonzero, then the absolute change in that weighted sum, divided by the absolute baseline weighted sum, is at most epsilon times the ratio of sum_i |ell_i f_i| to the absolute baseline weighted sum. The assertion is purely conditional and contains no existentially quantified witness.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: There is no explicit hypothesis epsilon >= 0. Nevertheless, the two stated hypotheses force epsilon >= 0: a nonzero weighted sum implies that some f_i is nonzero, and for that coordinate a negative epsilon would make the nonnegative number |deltaF_i| bounded above by a negative number. Thus the proposition is vacuous for epsilon < 0.
Although n = 0 is universally included, the sum over Fin 0 is the empty sum 0, so the nonzero baseline hypothesis is impossible. The proposition is therefore vacuous in dimension zero.
Because the statement is a chain of implications, it asserts nothing when either the componentwise perturbation condition or the nonzero baseline condition fails.
If f_i = 0, the componentwise hypothesis forces deltaF_i = 0.
The nonzero hypothesis concerns only the baseline weighted sum. The perturbed weighted sum is not required to be nonzero.
No upper bound such as epsilon < 1 is imposed.
The weights ell_i and entries f_i are otherwise arbitrary real numbers; there are no positivity, normalization, or nonvanishing assumptions on individual coordinates.
The perturbation model is componentwise relative error, not a bound in a vector norm.

The proposition describes exact real arithmetic and an exact finite weighted sum. It encodes no floating-point format, rounding operation, algorithm, probabilistic model, or representability condition.
Lean's real division is total even at zero, but the nonzero baseline hypothesis ensures that both denominators relevant to the conclusion are genuinely nonzero.
